title: Change creates questions
governing_claim: A changed instruction or interpretation creates impact-review candidates and new evidence needs; it does not automatically rewrite downstream behaviour or historical evidence.
memory_handle: Change creates questions before it creates truth
reader_success: Identify the exact proposition that changed.
Trace which downstream objects may require review without assuming they changed automatically.
Explain why historical evidence remains pinned to its original version and scope.
Identify the human decision and new evidence required before controlled content changes.

steps.claim: Start with the proposition that changed.
steps.salient: The semantic delta is explicit: the candidate revision adds a source-date requirement.
steps.hold_fixed: The candidate is not approved and does not silently supersede version 1.
steps.false_inference_risk: A side-by-side version view can imply a completed replacement rather than a proposal.

steps.claim: Dependency creates impact-review candidates, not automatic updates.
steps.salient: Requirement, mapping and test are linked as review candidates with typed relationship meaning.
steps.hold_fixed: Current object content remains unchanged until a responsible review decides otherwise.
steps.false_inference_risk: Spatial fan-out can be read as a propagation engine rather than a review map.

steps.claim: Review the expected behaviour, not only the document version.
steps.salient: The reader can identify what behaviour, mapping or test expectation would need to change and what remains stable.
steps.hold_fixed: Implementation remains not supplied unless actual implementation evidence exists.
steps.false_inference_risk: A redline can make a proposed expected behaviour look implemented.

steps.claim: Evidence belongs to the version and scope that produced it.
steps.salient: The historical evidence record remains visibly on the version-1 side of the fault line.
steps.hold_fixed: No previous record is rebound to version 2.
steps.false_inference_risk: Historical evidence may be mistaken for a previous pass even when no observed result is supplied.

steps.claim: A revised claim needs relevant new evidence.
steps.salient: The evidence gap is a first-class object in the explanation rather than whitespace the design silently completes.
steps.hold_fixed: A proposed test, empty evidence record or old result is not an observed pass for the revision.
steps.false_inference_risk: A polished evidence panel can still imply assurance unless the missing result is explicit.

steps.claim: Controlled change ends in a human decision and an evidence plan.
steps.salient: Confirm meaning/applicability, responsible reviewers, implementation intent and what evidence must be collected next.
steps.hold_fixed: No owner or approval is invented where the supplied context does not establish one.
steps.false_inference_risk: A final decision node can imply that the decision has already been made.
